mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average predicts a positive S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as improved housing demand offsets broader consumption weakness.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises above its 12-month moving average signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and cost-push inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% for four consecutive months, coupled with a federal funds rate below 2%, indicates a delayed monetary policy response that erodes real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5% for 4 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly retail sales index (RSAFS) rising above its 12-month moving average while GDP growth (GDPC1) is negative predicts a positive S&P 500 return over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate a near-term rebound in consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA AND GDPC1 < 0 (quarterly, most recent)
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises signals a mismatch between labor market quantity and quality, reducing productivity and compressing margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a sustained weakness in residential construction demand, which reduces related equity earnings and confidence, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
